rules.status: Useful if a dietary gap exists
rules.reason: Protein powder can help fill a known dietary protein gap. If food already meets your needs, adding powder is optional.
Creatine monohydrate has evidence for repeated high-intensity exercise and resistance-training adaptations. It is not required to begin training.
Low fish intake is a reason to review dietary omega-3 sources, not proof that a fish-oil supplement will prevent disease. Compare verified EPA+DHA.
Some short trials suggest benefits for stress or sleep with specific extracts. Long-term safety and equivalence across products remain uncertain.
A bone-health goal alone does not establish vitamin D deficiency or justify a high-strength product. Confirm the need and suitable formulation with a clinician.

rules.status: Not an automatic sleep or recovery add-on
rules.reason: Review dietary intake and an established reason for supplementation. A salt name or elemental amount does not establish a sleep benefit.
Assess calcium, magnesium and zinc separately. A combined tablet is not automatically better than addressing an individual dietary gap.

rules.status: Limited evidence: review the claim first
rules.reason: Small oral trials report mixed biomarker and cosmetic findings. They do not establish a general detox, disease-prevention or lasting skin-lightening benefit. Discuss a specific concern with a dermatologist; no product is added automatically.

rules.status: Review the sleep problem and timing first
rules.reason: Melatonin is relevant to some circadian problems, not every poor night or chronic insomnia. Timing, release form, medicines and the cause of sleep difficulty need review. It is not automatically combined with other sleep supplements.

rules.status: Check the need and laboratory-test implications
rules.reason: Evidence for routine hair or nail benefits without biotin deficiency is limited. Biotin can distort some laboratory tests. Review the cause of symptoms and disclose all biotin products to the testing team; no pack is added automatically.

rules.status: Review dietary supply before adding strength
rules.reason: Vitamin C can address inadequate intake, but routine high-strength use is not a general cold-prevention plan. Review food sources, clinical context and overlapping ingredients before choosing a product.

B vitamins are distinct nutrients; a B-complex is not a diagnosis or an automatic energy treatment. People avoiding animal foods need a reliable B12 source. Review individual needs, possible absorption issues and total B6 or niacin before adding products.

rules.status: Review folate form and the reason for use
rules.reason: Folic acid has a specific prevention role for women who could become pregnant; it is not interchangeable with every folate form or DFE label. Discuss an appropriate plan and B12 context with a clinician. The tool does not prescribe a pregnancy product or strength.
